citation: Dan I. Slobin (1996), From thought and language to thinking for speaking, in Rethinking Linguistic Relativity, pp. 70-96
bounded_use: Speech planning repeatedly recruits language-specific packaging choices.
limitations: A framework for language use, not proof that language determines all thought.

citation: Caitlin M. Fausey et al. (2010), Constructing Agency: The Role of Language, Frontiers in Psychology 1:162
bounded_use: English/Japanese accidental-event descriptions and later agent memory differed in the tested tasks; language priming shifted memory.
limitations: Task, sample and culture-language covariation limit generalization; no national responsibility conclusion.

citation: Silvia P. Gennari et al. (2002), Motion events in language and cognition, Cognition 83(1):49-79
bounded_use: Some English/Spanish similarity effects appeared after verbal encoding, while nonlinguistic encoding and recognition were similar.
limitations: Does not establish persistent perceptual restructuring.

citation: Anna Papafragou et al. (2008), Does language guide event perception? Evidence from eye movements, Cognition 108(1):155-184
bounded_use: Language-specific attention appeared when preparing to speak; ordinary nonlinguistic perception did not show the same online pattern, with later memory effects in some tasks.
limitations: Effects depend on task timing and encoding demands.

citation: Anna Papafragou, Christine Massey and Lila Gleitman (2002), Shake, rattle, 'n' roll: The representation of motion in language and cognition, Cognition 84(2):189-219
bounded_use: Different motion descriptions coexisted with similar nonlinguistic memory and categorization in the tested tasks.
limitations: A null result in bounded tasks, not proof that language never affects cognition.

citation: Yaying Ji and Anna Papafragou (2026), The representation of event boundedness in English and Mandarin speakers, Cognition 271:106443
bounded_use: English/Mandarin linguistic telicity patterns differed while endpoint likelihood and nonverbal temporal judgments were similar in the reported experiments.
limitations: Specific tasks and varieties; does not settle all aspect-cognition questions.

citation: Evelina Fedorenko and Rosemary Varley (2016), Language and thought are not the same thing, Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences 1369(1):132-153
bounded_use: Neuropsychological and neuroimaging evidence supports dissociation between core language mechanisms and multiple domains of thought.
limitations: Does not imply language is irrelevant to task-specific cognition.

citation: Charles N. Li and Sandra A. Thompson (1981), Mandarin Chinese: A Functional Reference Grammar
bounded_use: Structural and discourse reference for bounded modern Mandarin profile.
limitations: A reference grammar is not a profile of every speaker, dialect, genre or period.

citation: Rodney Huddleston and Geoffrey K. Pullum (2002), The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language
bounded_use: Structural reference for contemporary standard written English profile.
limitations: Does not exhaust dialect, conversation, genre or literary variation.

citation: Masayoshi Shibatani (1990), The Languages of Japan
bounded_use: Structural spine for bounded Japanese contrast profile.
limitations: Pilot still requires current native-speaker and genre-specific adjudication.

citation: Aslı Göksel and Celia Kerslake (2025), Turkish: A Comprehensive Grammar, second edition
bounded_use: Structural spine for bounded modern standard Turkish contrast profile.
limitations: Pilot lacks full native publication adjudication and does not cover all varieties.

citation: WALS Online, Chapter 81 Order of Subject, Object and Verb, language datapoints and chapter cautions
bounded_use: Narrow canonical word-order comparison for Mandarin, English, Japanese and Turkish.
limitations: Canonical order covers a restricted clause type; flexible orders are pragmatically constrained and labels do not define a whole language.

citation: WALS Online, Chapter 78 Coding of Evidentiality
bounded_use: Cross-language location of grammaticalized evidential distinctions, especially Turkish comparison.
limitations: Coarse typology does not settle context-sensitive meanings or competing analyses.

citation: Lars Johanson (2018), Turkic indirectivity, in The Oxford Handbook of Evidentiality
bounded_use: Bounded account of Turkic indirect/evidential systems and contextual functions.
limitations: Morphology does not itself establish source reliability or speaker belief.

citation: Seckin Arslan et al. (2015), Processing grammatical evidentiality and time reference in Turkish heritage and monolingual speakers, Frontiers in Psychology 6:1387
bounded_use: Demonstrates processing relevance and speaker-group variation for Turkish grammatical evidentiality/time reference in tested tasks.
limitations: Does not justify a universal Turkish cognitive profile.

citation: Beryl Hoffman (1997), Word order, information structure, and discourse relations in Turkish
bounded_use: Turkish word-order variation is related to information structure and discourse rather than arbitrary permutation.
limitations: Specific analytic framework; construction and context variation remains.

citation: Nerida Jarkey (2021), Japanese social relations and honorific language
bounded_use: Honorific choices encode socially situated relations and viewpoints.
limitations: Use varies by setting, ideology, irony, profession and individual choice.

citation: Cassie L. Liardét (2016), Nominalization and grammatical metaphor: Elaborating the theory, English for Specific Purposes 44:16-29
bounded_use: Nominalization is a functional academic resource whose effects depend on use, not an automatic style defect.
limitations: Does not license agency-obscuring nominalization or define all English registers.

citation: Task 114 plural Chinese literary calibration: Wang Zengqi, Lu Xun, Lao She, Shen Congwen, Zhu Ziqing, Sun Li, A Cheng and Shi Tiesheng; mechanism-level descriptions only
bounded_use: Demonstrates multiple lawful Chinese sentence organizations and tests anti-homogenization.
limitations: No author cloning, no large corpus, no claim that writers define grammar or universal literary quality.
